app.notes: Sophosia is a Tauri v1 + Vue 3/Quasar desktop app with no web backend; its UI talks to Rust via the Tauri IPC. Setup: mise.toml pins node 22.14.0 + yarn 1.22.22; `yarn install --no-default-rc --use-yarnrc .yarnrc --frozen-lockfile --ignore-engines` (the parent-dir .npmrc walk hits an unreadable ~/.npmrc otherwise; optional canvas fails to build, harmless); `npx quasar build` -> dist/spa. .ui-capture/server (npm: better-sqlite3, @fontsource-variable/dm-sans) is the local host. Data: .ui-capture/seed/seed.mjs writes a workspace in the app's own on-disk format at /home/dana/Documents/Sophosia (project folders with folder-note JSON meta, generated multi-page PDFs, markdown + Excalidraw notes, .sophosia/{appState,layout,pdfAnnotation} JSON, workspace.json in the app config dir), then seed/build-data.sh runs the real front end headlessly so the app's own indexer builds its SQLite FTS index, and freezes the result in .ui-capture/data-snapshot. start.sh restores that snapshot on each start (so state is reset every run) and serves on $PORT. Persona: Dana, 4th-year PhD student in clinical NLP / efficient transformers. Library: 62 projects (real papers and textbooks with authors, venues, DOIs, paraphrased abstracts; 2 half-filled/'New Project' entries), nested categories (Thesis/Ch2..Ch5, NLP/*, Clinical NLP, Reading Group/Fall 2026, Books, Teaching...), tags, favorites, added dates spread from late 2024 to Nov 2026 (8 in the last 30 days for 'Added'), 24 attached PDFs, 34 markdown notes (reading notes, run logs with tables, LaTeX, TODOs, reading-group minutes, TA plans; one subfolder), 3 Excalidraw diagrams, 35 PDF highlights/underlines with comments, 23 note->project links for the related-items graph. Main areas: left sidebar (opened projects tree with notes, category tree), Library page (Library/Added/Favorite tabs, meta and full-text search, right-side meta info panel), PDF reader (EmbedPDF) with annotations, markdown note editor (Vditor), Excalidraw page, graph view, settings (theme, citation keys, plugins with community list), workspace switcher. Tabs open on start: Library, a PDF (Li_2023 Clinical-Longformer) and Mamba 'Reading notes.md'. Bridge detail: SQL plugin calls are queued in issue order in bridge.js (Tauri's IPC is a single ordered channel; the app fires author INSERTs without awaiting). Rebuild everything: yarn install (flags above) -> npx quasar build -> (cd .ui-capture/server && npm ci) -> .ui-capture/seed/build-data.sh (needs the local Playwright chromium_headless_shell; only for re-seeding, not at runtime).

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):

- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com).
